correctness.rationale: For all integers q,d>=2, graph automorphism averaging preserves feasibility and does not increase centered spectral norm. Fourier diagonalization explicitly yields every eigenvalue for the invariant two-orbit kernels. d=2 is complete; d=3 has the sharp three-contact interpolation bound 1/7 and the first-character alternative for q>=5; d>=4,q=2 follows from degree-one and parity contacts; d>=4,q>=3 uses a degree-one lower bound, convex-quadratic endpoint checks, a general lower estimate for d>=5, and explicit four-mode comparison at d=4. Every mass is nonnegative and normalized, every spectral mode bounded. Nearest-neighbor comparison is proved independently by linear Fourier endpoints. Standalone exact-rational, independent LP, and full-matrix tests passed 5,172 assertions; infinite cases are proved analytically.

value.rationale: The natural unrestricted symmetric design problem for the radius-two Hamming graph gains a complete two-parameter exact classification with adjacent q=4 and q=5 transitions at d=3, an exact holding and orbit-usage phase structure, and a sharp factor-two improvement over the optimal nearest-neighbor spectral gap for every alphabet and every dimension >=4. These facts guide concrete randomized updates in product-state networks and are not a routine one-parameter reformulation of the nearest-neighbor formula. No equal computational-cost or finite-time total-variation gain is claimed.
